Use or input class: Problem framing, brainstorming and alternative generation
Status and boundary: Conditional. Use only within the applicable rule. The student must formulate the decision problem and retain authority over selection. Authority: D1, D2 and D4.
Minimum control and evidence: Record the task, alternatives received, rejected options, selection rationale and effect on the project. Verify factual premises before they influence scope.
Block, stop or reopen when: Block adoption if the output defines the problem without student judgement, imports unverifiable assumptions or cannot be explained at the Problem Gate.

Use or input class: Outlining, drafting, translation and language correction
Status and boundary: Conditional. Form-only assistance is lower risk only while it does not add content, alter meaning or conceal authorship. Current disclosure rules still apply. Authority: D1, D2 and D4.
Minimum control and evidence: Compare before and after, inspect every retained passage, verify terminology and sources and record any consequential change to argument or claim.
Block, stop or reopen when: Revert or rewrite if meaning shifted, a claim was added, uncertainty was suppressed or the student cannot defend the retained wording.

Status and boundary: Conditional. Treat outputs as leads, never as evidence or a bibliographic authority. Authority: D1, D2 and D5.
Minimum control and evidence: Resolve each item in an authoritative catalogue, publisher page, DOI registry or primary source. Read the source actually cited and record the search route where consequential.
Block, stop or reopen when: Delete unresolved references. One fabricated item triggers an audit of the whole AI-mediated source set and every dependent claim.

Use or input class: Synthesis, review, gap identification and claim drafting
Status and boundary: High-risk conditional use. The system may assist comparison but must not replace source reading, eligibility decisions, appraisal, extraction or inference. Authority: D1–D4.
Minimum control and evidence: Retain source-to-claim links, extraction evidence, counter-evidence and the student’s synthesis memo. Verify quotations and summaries against the original text.
Block, stop or reopen when: Reopen the Evidence or Claim Gate when a synthesis cannot be reconstructed from controlled sources independently of the generated prose.

Use or input class: Code generation, debugging and technical configuration
Status and boundary: High-risk conditional use. Generated code is untrusted candidate code. Authority: D1, D2 and D5.
Minimum control and evidence: Inspect the code, dependencies and licences; run unit, integration, security and failure tests appropriate to the risk; preserve the accepted diff and test evidence; explain every material component.
Block, stop or reopen when: Quarantine code that is untested, insecure, licence-incompatible, non-reproducible or not understood by the student.

Use or input class: Data analysis, statistical interpretation and quantitative claims
Status and boundary: High-risk conditional use. Narrative output is not a calculation and a model’s confidence is not uncertainty analysis. Authority: D1, D2 and D5.
Minimum control and evidence: Reproduce every result from controlled data and executable analysis, check assumptions, units, denominators and sensitivity and retain the script, environment and output snapshot.
Block, stop or reopen when: Reopen the Design, Execution or Claim Gate if the result cannot be reproduced without the generative system.

Use or input class: Synthetic data, generated images, audio or other artefacts
Status and boundary: Conditional. They must be labelled, justified and kept distinct from observed data or documentary evidence. Rights and representational risks apply. Authority: D2, D3 and D5.
Minimum control and evidence: Record purpose, generator, model or version where available, prompt or procedure, seed or settings where applicable, provenance, limitations, licence review and separation from empirical records.
Block, stop or reopen when: Do not use generated material as if observed, measured, consented or historically authentic. Unresolved provenance or rights blocks release.

Use or input class: Meetings, interviews, transcription and third-party material
Status and boundary: Conditional and potentially restricted. Permission, privacy, confidentiality, research-ethics and third-party terms govern. Authority: D1 and D2.
Minimum control and evidence: Inform affected parties where required, use an authorised environment, minimise input, check the transcript against the recording and inspect received files for hidden text, metadata or embedded instructions.
Block, stop or reopen when: Do not upload protected material by default. Stop processing when authority, notice, consent or data handling is inadequate.

Use or input class: Personal, confidential, unpublished, licensed or security-sensitive input
Status and boundary: Mandatory boundary. Do not transmit it to an external, public or institutionally unvalidated system. An approved governed environment may be used only within documented authority. Authority: D1–D3.
Minimum control and evidence: Classify the input first, apply data minimisation and access control and retain the authorisation, environment and purpose. A provider opt-out setting does not itself create permission.
Block, stop or reopen when: Stop immediately after unauthorised disclosure, preserve an incident record and follow the competent institutional, controller or security procedure.

Use or input class: Fabrication, falsification, invented evidence or plagiarism concealment
Status and boundary: Mandatory prohibition. This includes invented participants, data, results, quotations or references and paraphrasing intended to disguise unattributed material. Authority: D1–D4.
Minimum control and evidence: No admissible control can convert fabrication into acceptable work. Verify provenance and attribution before retention.
Block, stop or reopen when: Remove the material, audit dependent sections and escalate under the applicable integrity procedure when the defect is material.

Use or input class: Confidential review, assessment or evaluation of another person’s work
Status and boundary: Mandatory restriction unless the competent process explicitly authorises a governed use. Substantial AI use can compromise confidentiality, fairness and independent judgement. Authority: D1–D3.
Minimum control and evidence: Keep protected submissions outside external systems and retain human responsibility for every evaluative judgement. Record any authorised tool use and its boundary.
Block, stop or reopen when: Do not delegate scientific assessment, peer review or grading to a generative system. Withdraw or correct a compromised evaluation through the competent route.

Status and boundary: Mandatory prohibition unless explicitly authorised in writing for that assessment. Authority: D1.
Minimum control and evidence: Prepare offline, verify rehearsal outputs and retain TRACE where consequential. During the assessment use only the aids expressly permitted by the controlling instructions.
Block, stop or reopen when: Hidden or unauthorised answer generation is substitution, not assistance. Stop use and follow the examination rule.
